Dark mode is chosen by the `dark` class, so it follows the setting you store, not only the system. Use the semantic utilities (`text-muted-foreground`, `text-destructive`), never a fixed colour, so both themes keep their contrast. Do not rely on colour alone: the status words in the examples ("Deployed", "Rolled back") carry the meaning.

Dark mode does nothing — the `dark` class must be on `<html>` (next-themes `attribute="class"`), not on `<body>`. A flash of the wrong theme on load — keep `suppressHydrationWarning` on `<html>` and let `ThemeProvider` set the class before paint. Utilities such as `bg-primary` have no effect — `styles.css` already imports Tailwind, so import it once and do not add a second `@import "tailwindcss"`. A colour looks wrong in dark — a fixed colour (`text-gray-500`) was used; switch to a semantic token. Red text is unreadable on a dark surface — `destructive` is a fill colour, so `text-destructive` on `bg-muted` fails contrast in dark mode; show status with `Badge variant="destructive"` or `Alert`.

needs.need: Pin a stage and change scene as the page scrolls
needs.audience: Developers telling a story in a few steps (one product shown in several looks, a feature tour, before/after) on a marketing or docs page.
needs.purpose: One stage stays under the header while the page scrolls; each scene fades in, holds, then fades out before the next. Pure CSS scroll-driven animation: no script, no scroll hijacking, native scrolling only.
needs.whenToUse: Two to eight (`SCROLL_SCENES_MAX`) short scenes that read well one at a time and where scrolling is the natural way to move on.
needs.whenNotToUse: Long content, forms or anything focusable inside a scene — invisible scenes stay in the accessibility tree, so keep scene visuals non-interactive (`aria-hidden` and `inert`); steps the user must pick themselves — use `Tabs` or `WizardSteps`.

examples.title: Pinned feature tour
Before and after

needs.a11y: Captions are real text in a fixed order and are never hidden (opacity only), so put the message in the caption and treat the visual as decoration: mark it `aria-hidden="true"` and `inert` so it adds no tab stop and no duplicate announcement. Under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`, in browsers without scroll timelines (Firefox, Safari before 26) and in very short windows, the scenes are plain blocks one under the other with the same content. A decorative progress rail is `aria-hidden`. Give each caption a heading one level under the section title so screen reader users can jump scene by scene.
needs.troubleshooting: Nothing is pinned — you need two to eight scenes, the browser needs `animation-timeline: view()` and the window at least 34rem tall; otherwise you get the stacked layout by design. Stage hides under a fixed header — set `--zk-scenes-top` to the header height. Scenes change too fast or slowly — set `--zk-scenes-step` (scroll distance per scene, default 60svh). Content cut at the bottom — the stage is one screen tall; shorten the scene or hide secondary parts on small screens. Pinning stops inside a box — a parent with `overflow: hidden` or `auto` becomes the scroll container; keep the component in the normal page flow. The scenes stack in your own preview — `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` is on in the OS or the browser; this is the intended fallback.
seeAlso: Switch between tabbed panels

needs.need: Switch the visual identity with one attribute
needs.audience: Teams that want to change the whole look of an app, or offer a choice, without touching components.
needs.purpose: `data-identity` on the root swaps the identity tokens next to light and dark (type size, tracking, shadow, spacing unit, body line-height, border width, colour-transition duration, radius, motion); a head script applies the stored choice before first paint and a labelled switcher or touch picker lets people choose. Mist keeps the kit defaults; no two looks share the same type size, tracking, shadow, or spacing unit.
needs.whenToUse: To rebrand or offer several looks from one set of components.
needs.whenNotToUse: For a single fixed brand — edit the base tokens in `styles.css` instead.

needs.a11y: `IdentitySwitcher` is a native labelled `select` (visible label with `showLabel`, otherwise screen-reader only); `IdentityPicker` is a 44px trigger opening a sheet with a labelled radio group. Both render nothing when there is no identity to choose. A choice applies at once and the new look keeps the kit's contrast pairs in light and dark; announce the change in your own status line (`role="status"`) if you show one. Keep the trigger name stable (`label`), because the current identity is read from the value.
needs.troubleshooting: The look flashes on load — render `<IdentityScript />` inside `<head>` with the same ids and storage key as the switcher, and `suppressHydrationWarning` on `<html>`. A stored id is ignored — it must be in `ids`. Built-in ids: `mist`, `press`, `tide`, `volt`, `maison`, `glass`; pass your own list to the script and the switcher to offer other looks. The whole page changed but you wanted one card — put `data-identity-scope` and `data-identity="…"` on that element instead of changing `<html>`; the scope sets tokens, fonts and radii for its subtree only. Two switchers disagree — give them the same `storageKey`; they follow each other through `IDENTITY_CHANGE_EVENT`.
